lesson_title: How a Goat Turned Into a R200 Note
hook_text: Your R200 note is just paper. So why will the shop give you food for it?
clip_script: Start with a goat. You swap it for grain: that is barter, and it only works if the farmer wants a goat. So villages picked something everyone valued, cattle, salt or beads: commodity money. But cows die and salt melts. Enter metal coins, stamped with their weight. They last, but a bag of coins is heavy and robbers love heavy bags. So you leave coins with a banker and get a paper promise to pay. People start trading the paper itself. Today the Reserve Bank issues the rand, and the law and our trust make that paper worth two hundred rand. Every step fixed a problem of the step before.
visual_style: A whiteboard timeline: a goat, a pile of beads, a stamped coin, a paper receipt and a R200 note, joined by arrows.
mood: Fast, funny and surprising, a history race in one minute.
pacing: Quick hops along the timeline, then a slow close on the rand note.
